summary.headline: Onida Q2 FY27 brand revenue rose 65% YoY to Rs 150.4 crore, with brand margin at 17.7%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 total revenue from operations was Rs 198.6 crore, up 22% YoY, while brand business revenue grew 65% to Rs 150.4 crore. H1 FY27 brand revenue rose 48% to Rs 325.7 crore and total revenue rose 25% to Rs 381.1 crore. Management said input cost inflation (copper, aluminium, steel, plastics, memory chips) squeezed sector margins, and it is relying on calibrated pricing, cost optimisation and mix to protect margins. Management guided to EBITDA breakeven at a gross margin of roughly 25-26%, but would not commit to FY27 EBITDA positivity.

financial_highlights.value: 17.8% vs 15% in H1 FY26, excluding one-offs

financial_highlights.change: Led by ACs and washing machines

segments.name: Air conditioners
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 AC business grew 239% YoY; Onida ACs gained e-commerce market share in September 2026 per sell-out data. Range for upcoming season finalised.

segments.name: LED televisions
segments.commentary: LED TV business grew 52% YoY in Q2 FY27. Launched a 100-inch QD Mini LED flagship. Entry-segment demand weakened on steep panel-driven price increases.

segments.name: Washing machines
segments.commentary: Portfolio being revamped; partly outsourced and partly made at Roorkee plant. E-commerce offering being completed.

segments.name: OEM business
segments.commentary: Being deliberately slowed; margin in low single digits versus high double-digit brand margin. Pending orders expected to run 8-12 months more with revenue decelerating.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B AC
segments.commentary: Early-stage vertical contributing low single digit revenue share in the current year, with leads now converting.

guidance_outlook: Management is optimistic on festive demand, citing sustained better buying over the last two to three weeks and an encouraging early sentiment.
EBITDA breakeven is expected if gross margin holds near 25-26%; management did not give a timeline for EBITDA positivity in FY27 and declined to confirm it.
Price increases will still leave an estimated 200-400 bps margin impact in some categories, not fully passed on.
Over the next two years management aims to outgrow the market from a lower base.
Service centre count (425) will be consolidated over the next 3-4 months rather than expanded further.
capex_capacity: Service network stands at 425 centres; expansion considered largely complete for FY27, with focus shifting to productivity.
Distribution: added 57 distributors and 127 direct dealers (another answer cited about 120); management said more than 50% of the roughly 4,000-outlet target was added in H1.
Onida Smarthub exclusive outlets: four operational, expansion under way via franchise model.
Roorkee plant to be strengthened for washing machines; AC and LED remain largely contract-manufactured.
Wada plant: VRS completed on a partial basis; plant operations being reduced; management said the settlement will not yield significant annual savings.
demand_pricing: Industry input cost inflation in H1 FY27 was steep; competitive intensity limited offset, so sector margins stayed under pressure.
Entry-segment TVs weakened on price hikes; premium and large-screen demand held up.
AC demand pickup is visible in West and South from summer heat; North and East remain weak in winter.
Management declined to quantify cumulative price hikes; said RM inflation is not stabilising in a predictable way.
Channel partners built inventory ahead of festive season; BEE norm transition in ACs largely complete.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 be EBITDA positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is pushing for it and that it is an internal objective, but would not give a firm answer. Breakeven depends on gross margin around 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Price hike magnitude and remaining RM offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Price increases were taken in calibrated steps over time and varied by category; management said some categories still carry a 200-400 bps impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is OEM business a drag on margins from past orders?
qa_highlights.answer: The company is deliberately slowing OEM; pending orders will run 8-12 months more, with revenue decelerating each quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for Chinese JV, compressor manufacturing or PLI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no plans for any tie-up with a Chinese or other brand, and has not communicated such plans in the last 6-7 months.

qa_highlights.question: Institutional AC sales progress?
qa_highlights.answer: The B2B institutional vertical made good progress in the last quarter; leads are converting and it is expected to contribute low single digit revenue this year.

qa_highlights.question: E-commerce share and tier-2/3 expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: E-commerce is about 8-10% of revenue, with market share slightly higher. Tier-2/3 reach comes via distributors, a rural distribution tie-up and Smarthub franchise outlets.

risks_watch: West Asia situation keeps commodity and component costs (copper, aluminium, steel, memory chips) rising; management is cautious on margins.
Management declined to quantify price hikes or ESOP vesting targets, limiting visibility on margin pass-through and governance metrics.
OEM revenue runs off over 8-12 months; the brand-only margin profile depends on brand growth replacing it.
Entry-segment TV demand is weak on panel-driven price increases.
Q3 festive sell-out and whether October's growth pace (described only as 'in line with past') continues.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line momentum and brand recovery, but cautious and non-committal on profitability, input costs and ESOP targets. Management repeatedly declined to quantify price hikes, FY27 EBITDA timing and ESOP tranche percentages.
key_quotes: We are absolutely thinking in the same lines as you said Aditya.
So, we have certain pending orders to be executed if I look from the timeline it will continue for another 8 to 12 months at the most.
we are hopeful that if the margin what we are earning currently if that continues probably at the level of 250 to 260 broad numbers I am giving it we should be able to EBITDA break even.

growth.why: Total revenue rose 22% YoY in Q2 FY27 (brand +65%, offset by OEM run-off and deliberate slowdown), with no revenue growth guidance; management is optimistic on festive demand but gives no numbers, offers EBITDA breakeven only if gross margin holds at 25-26% (not firm), and declined to commit to FY27 EBITDA positivity.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Brand revenue grew 65% YoY to Rs 150.4 crore in Q2 FY27 and H1 brand revenue rose 48% to Rs 325.7 crore; distribution added 57 distributors and 127 dealers, with over 50% of the ~4,000-outlet target reached in H1, though OEM volumes are running off.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Service and distribution expansion is largely complete for FY27 with focus shifting to productivity, and no new plant or capex quantum was discussed.

rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance was raised; management is optimistic on festive demand but gives no numbers and declined to commit to FY27 EBITDA positivity.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on input costs (copper, aluminium, steel, memory chips) that it says are not stabilising predictably, and the breakeven gross margin of 25-26% is not firm.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AC range for the upcoming season is finalised and a 100-inch QD Mini LED flagship has launched; washing machine portfolio revamp and e-commerce offering are being completed.

rows.label: OEM run-off decelerating

rows.label: Onida Smarthub franchise outlets

rows.label: Institutional / B2B AC vertical

tone.note: Management was confident on brand top-line momentum (brand revenue +65% YoY) and festive demand, but cautious and non-committal on FY27 EBITDA positivity, input costs and price-hike magnitude; analysts pressed on the EBITDA timing and remaining RM offset.
